findings.statement: The North Carolina Secretary of State business registry could not be searched: both the business registration search path and the sosnc.gov host returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge token, so the registry blocks automation and no authoritative search for 'Brian Lighting LLC' or for the events business named in the declared domain was possible. A general web search surfaced many sosnc.gov entity profiles but none named 'Brian Lighting LLC'. This leaves the core entity-type mismatch unresolved: the account is declared btype Individual while the business name asserts 'LLC', and those cannot both be true. The NC Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors public register at arls-public.ncbeec.org loads but is token and JavaScript driven; a scripted query returned an empty form even for a broad control search, so no real licence search was executed and the absence of a lighting or electrical contractor licence is NOT established here. Both the registry and the licence check must be done manually before this dimension can be scored.
findings.establishes: Neither the NC entity registry nor the NC electrical contractor licence register could be queried, so the asserted-LLC-with-declared-Individual mismatch is unresolved rather than cleared.

findings.statement: No independent listing, social page, directory entry or address/phone of any kind places a business called 'Brian Lighting LLC' in Wilmington NC, or anywhere else. The only Wilmington NC footprint attached to any identifier on this account belongs to a different business: a wedding planning and event design firm listed at Wilmington, NC on The Knot under the trade name used by the declared domain. A furniture or home-furnishings retailer (the declared MCC 5712) and a lighting installer are both trades requiring licensed physical premises, and neither has any observable footprint under the declared business name.
findings.establishes: The declared business name has zero independent operating footprint; the only Wilmington presence belongs to an unrelated third-party business.

findings.statement: The representative does not match the publicly named owner of the business at the declared website and statement descriptor. That business's own site and its vendor page both identify a different individual as owner and lead designer, the site's published contact address is in that other individual's name, and all seven customer reviews refer to that other individual as the planner. The representative's name appears nowhere on that site, on any review reply, listing, licence record or news item, and no public source links the representative either to that events business or to 'Brian Lighting LLC'. The representative shares a surname with the events-business owner, but a surname echo is not corroboration. Stripe reports legal_entity_verification_status verified, so no uplift applies; the contradiction stands on the public record alone.
findings.establishes: The business whose domain and descriptor this account declares is publicly owned by a different named person, and the representative is linked by no public source to that business or to the account's declared business name.

findings.statement: anobleevents.com resolves (HTTP 200) but belongs to a different business: the page title is 'A. Noble Events & Design' and the copy describes a full-service luxury event planning and design firm servicing the Southeast, with a contact address on that domain and social links to a matching events page. Nothing on the site mentions 'Brian Lighting LLC', lighting, or furniture. The statement descriptor ANOBLEEVENTS.COM likewise does not match the account's business name, so a cardholder paying 'Brian Lighting LLC' would see an unrelated event-planning domain on their statement, and the account email handle brianlighting01@gmail.com matches neither.
findings.establishes: The declared website and statement descriptor belong to a third-party event-planning firm, not to the account's declared business.

findings.statement: MCC 5712 is furniture and home-furnishings retail, which implies an observable goods inventory and retail premises. Nothing observable supports it: the declared URL sells full-service luxury wedding, corporate and life event planning and design services, a service business that would fall under event or party planning, not furniture retail. The business name and email handle instead describe lighting, a third and different trade. Three identifiers point at three incompatible business models - furniture retail, event services and lighting - and the MCC matches none of the observable activity.
findings.establishes: The declared MCC is incoherent with every observable business activity associated with the account's identifiers.

findings.statement: No dated reviews, listings, filings, news items, complaints or scam/fraud reports were found for 'Brian Lighting LLC' under that name. The verifiable multi-year trading history that does exist belongs to the third-party business at the declared URL, not to this merchant: its vendor page carries seven dated five-star reviews, one referencing a wedding postponed from May to August because of the coronavirus, placing that business's presence back to at least 2020. No adverse reports were found against either business or against the representative. The merchant as declared has no independent history of its own.
findings.establishes: No trading history exists for the declared business name; the established history belongs to an unrelated third party.

evidenceNeeded: Manual browser search of the NC Secretary of State business registry at sosnc.gov for 'Brian Lighting LLC', 'Brian Lighting', 'A Noble Events' and 'Noble Events' - the portal returned HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenges to automation, so the registration status and the Individual-vs-LLC entity-type mismatch remain unresolved.

Manual search of the NC Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors public licence register at arls-public.ncbeec.org/Public/Search for 'Brian Lighting' and for the representative - the form is token and JavaScript driven and did not execute programmatically, so no conclusion about a required electrical contractor licence can be drawn.

Written explanation from the merchant of why the declared website and statement descriptor (ANOBLEEVENTS.COM) belong to a third-party wedding-planning firm with a different public owner, while the account trades as 'Brian Lighting LLC' with email brianlighting01@gmail.com - plus documentary proof of the representative's authority over that domain if the descriptor is to stand.

Establish the relationship, if any, between the account representative and the publicly named owner of the events business, and whether this is an authorised sub-merchant or white-label arrangement or an unrelated party using another business's domain and descriptor.
Proof of the actual goods or services sold and a corresponding MCC correction - MCC 5712 (furniture/home furnishings) matches neither event planning nor lighting.
Manual review of the events business's Facebook and Instagram pages and of any Google Business Profile, to check for owner-reply evidence naming the account representative.
summary: This account presents three mutually incompatible identities with no verified link between them: the registered name 'Brian Lighting LLC' (a lighting trade, with a matching gmail handle), the declared website and statement descriptor anobleevents.com (a Wilmington NC luxury wedding and event planning firm), and MCC 5712 for furniture and home-furnishings retail. The website resolves and is genuine, but it belongs to an events business publicly owned by a different named individual, with seven dated five-star reviews going back to at least 2020 - not to the account representative, whose name appears nowhere on that business, on any licence record, or on any trace of 'Brian Lighting LLC', which has no independent footprint whatsoever. The surname overlap between the representative and the events-business owner is the only connection found and is not corroboration. Total risk 39, driven by identity (12), operating (10) and contact (10); the legal dimension scores 0 only because the NC Secretary of State registry and the NC electrical contractor licence register both blocked automated searches, so the entity-type mismatch is unresolved rather than cleared. Hold payouts and obtain a merchant explanation of the descriptor mismatch plus manual registry checks before enabling volume.
